title: Capacity changes batch count
hook: Twenty things to carry: does a six- or eight-object carrier need fewer trips?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate whole batch counts using a stated usable capacity.

misconception: A fractional last batch can be ignored when counting trips.
objective: Calculate whole batch counts using a stated usable capacity.

claims.text: Ideal carriers hold exactly six or eight identical objects. Objects cannot be split; capacity is assumed usable. Scaled model; ideal usable capacities; no weight or safety claim.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Objects=20, A=4batches and B=3batches. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["ceil",["/","x",6]]; B=["ceil",["/","x",8]]; x denotes Objects. At x=20, A=4, B=3. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Divide object count by usable capacity and round up. The partial final batch still counts as a complete trip in this quantity-only model. Volume, weight and safe carrying limits would require separate constraints.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["ceil",["/","x",6]]; B=["ceil",["/","x",8]]; x denotes Objects. At x=20, A=4, B=3. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Ideal carriers hold exactly eight identical objects, which cannot be split. How many batches do 25 objects need? Correct: 4. 25 ÷ 8 = 3.125, and the partial last batch is still a whole trip: 4.
